body:
When a design agent proposes a change, nothing is visible until the human presses Accept, so the human has nothing to judge it by. The human asked to drop the Accept/Reject step: the agent's change is saved straight away as a new version that the human can look at. If they don't want it, they go back to an earlier version.

## Asked for

- Every design agent change becomes a new version of the design as soon as it's made, with no Accept or Reject step.
- The page can show what changed compared with the version before it (see the follow-on task for the controls).

## Done when

- A design run's change is checked and saved as a new version with the run as its source, and no question is put to the human. A new design gets its first version the same way.
- An invalid change is refused as it is today, and nothing is saved.
- The design page shows the new version without a reload.
- D-243 is amended (it currently requires Accept). Spec 15 and the design agent's brief and help say changes are saved as versions.

## Calls made

- A change to a design that got a newer version after the agent read it is still refused, and the agent reads the design again. This keeps D-243 point 2's rule that a later change is never lost.

## Not in this task

- task:08eb320c615ec583 (check before proposing) stays as it is. It still saves the agent from making versions that get refused.
title: design agent: changes saved as versions
